_comment: Cross-language contract for printer bindings (XCT-050, BAN-426).
This fixture exists because the two sides of this wire had never met. `PosPrinterRow`
`printer_ip`, `is_receipt_printer` and a pivot; and `posLoadFields()` returned ['*'], so
the raw columns shipped under their own names. Every field the register read came back
undefined: a receipt printer was classified `prep`, `categoryIds` was undefined, and the
first prep ticket of the shift threw a TypeError inside `resolveTargets`. No test on
either side could see it, because the only fixtures were hand-written to the declared
shape rather than to what the server sends.
So `printers` below is what the bootstrap must ship — PrinterBindingContractTest asserts
the real endpoint's payload carries exactly these field names and these derivations — and
`bindings` and `routing` are what the register must then make of them, asserted by
Either side drifting fails one of the two.

printers._why: Front-of-house receipt printer over Epson ePOS. No port set, so the address is the bare IP.
printers.name: Imprimante caisse (salle)

printers._why: Hot kitchen, network ESC/POS on 9100, routed by category. Address joins ip and port.
printers.name: Imprimante cuisine chaude

printers._why: Bar, routed by its own categories only.
printers.name: Imprimante bar

printers._why: The pass: prints every category. Distinct from an empty category list, which is only a fallback — this one must print a drink the bar is already printing.
printers.name: Imprimante passe

routing.why: A starter goes to the hot kitchen AND the pass. Before allCategories existed the pass was demoted to a fallback and printed nothing whenever a specific printer matched — the pass would have missed every course of every service.
A drink goes to the bar and the pass, not to the kitchen.
A category no printer claims still reaches the pass, because print-all matches before the fallback rule is ever consulted.

A receipt goes to the one receipt printer. This is the case that silently regressed: with print_receipt undefined every printer was prep, so no receipt target existed and the placeholder browser sink was invented on a till that has four real printers.
